questions: Reproduce source section 2.8 and distinguish useful effective rungs from repeated dispatches.
Compare per-provider evidence with cumulative failure counts and reset semantics.
decision: Define a pure effective-dispatch ladder that removes no-op rungs, retains failure-specific retry semantics and leaves provider switching to its dedicated integration tasks.
code_observations: choose_route derives a provider slot from total functional failures, whereas availability.select rebuilds a chain for the escalated tier. This can mismatch the ladder and dispatched provider.
The current exhaustion decision uses accumulated failure classes against a later provider's ladder, allowing that provider to be considered exhausted before its first attempt.
A logical tier/effort increase can resolve to the same model and native effort, especially with embedded effort slugs and equal strong/max models.

implementation_steps: Define a pure effective-dispatch identity after tier lifting, snapshot/profile resolution, effective effort and backend aliases, with no secrets.
Build useful ordered rungs by collapsing every known-equivalent effective dispatch, including non-adjacent aliases; preserve first occurrence and the requested capability floor.
Test pure classified transitions with provider/phase-local fixture evidence; do not persist new state or change runner dispatch in this task.
Retain the original legacy replay fixtures and disabled-mode argv assertions without weakening them.
Expose the primitives for 072 and 074; those tasks own durable counters, reset, availability integration and attempt reservation.
Build pure effective candidate identities after aliases, snapshots and native effort resolution; deduplicate equivalent rungs.
Test classified failure transitions per provider and phase without changing legacy-disabled behavior.
Keep full provider switching in TODOs 070-080; expose reusable ladder primitives and counterfactual dispatch fixtures here.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Pure ladder fixtures deduplicate resolved model/native-effort identities while preserving capability floors.
Pure transitions distinguish provider-local functional evidence from quota and environmental outcomes.
Legacy-disabled argv and routing fixtures remain unchanged; runtime integration is deferred to 072-074.
Different tier labels resolving to the same model and effective effort produce one capability rung.
An ignored effort argument does not count as increased capability.
A quota or environment failure does not advance the functional ladder.
The default disabled option preserves existing argv and routing fixtures.
Changing only quota pool, request nonce or log path cannot create a new capability rung.
Non-adjacent aliases for the same effective dispatch do not recreate a failed top attempt.

cost_model: Measure distinct useful attempts, repeated-top attempts and validated outcomes; expected benefit is avoided identical failed dispatches, not a claimed percentage of model-quality improvement.
unverified: Quality equivalence across providers is not established by matching tier labels. Real-run calibration remains an authorized evaluation step.
Public ranking and accepted CLI flags cannot establish equivalent intelligence across harnesses. Live backend identity may require a permitted response field or account-side verification.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Introduce a pure effective-dispatch ladder model with provider-local evidence; keep the legacy path unchanged until the opt-in switch policy is integrated.
revision_delta: The new research strengthens the distinction between logical tier and actual dispatch. It adds alias/backend identity, duplicate rungs with different nominal labels, and a counterfactual test for the claimed benefit of escalation.
decision_analysis: The baseline applies one global failure sequence to a provider-specific ladder, then availability may dispatch elsewhere. A cost-efficient fix starts with a pure representation of the actual candidate: harness, backend endpoint identity, resolved model, effective effort and relevant execution options. A logical tier change that leaves this representation unchanged is not additional capability.

Deduplicate all known-equivalent candidates, preserving their first occurrence, after all overrides, snapshots and embedded-effort rules are applied. Do not use a hardcoded provider ranking. Some role aliases map to the same backend, while an accepted effort flag can be ignored by a compatible endpoint. Record requested and resolved values separately; an unknown resolution is an explicit capability gap, not a license to guess.

Retain one bounded same-rung retry for a reproducible mechanical or budget failure only when the declared policy allows it. Semantic failure advances to the next distinct credible capability. Environmental, permission, plan-defect and fixed-time-limit failures do not establish a stronger model will help. Counter state belongs to provider and phase, not an aggregate inherited by a provider that has never run.

Learned routers and self-verification cascades solve a related but different problem from stateful retry routing. Keep their learned score out of the acceptance path. First test deterministic invariants and dispatch uniqueness on the existing fixtures; evaluate learned selection in shadow mode only after there is representative labeled evidence.

baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
identity_contract: Keep capability identity separate from availability identity: changing only a quota pool, request ID, log path or credential reference cannot create a stronger rung. Resolve known aliases and native effort before deduplication; retain the harness/backend boundary rather than equating model-family names across hosts.
